heroData.title: EOR in Kazakhstan
heroData.subtitle: Hire in Almaty & Astana
heroData.description: Compliant employment in Central Asia's largest economy. We handle everything from registration on the Enbek portal to 2025 social tax and mandatory pension contributions.

steps.title: Employment Agreement
steps.description: Drafting of the contract in both Kazakh and Russian languages. This is a mandatory requirement for all local hires.

steps.title: Enbek.kz Registration
steps.description: Mandatory registration of the employment contract on the Unified Employment Agreements Accounting System (UEAAS) within 5 working days of signing.

steps.title: IIN & Personal ID
steps.description: Obtaining an Individual Identification Number (IIN) for foreign residents or verifying the existing IIN for local citizens for tax filing.

steps.title: Medical Examination
steps.description: Ensuring the employee undergoes a preliminary medical check if the role involves heavy labor, hazardous conditions, or food services.

steps.title: Workplace Safety Induction
steps.description: Conducting mandatory health and safety training as required by the Kazakhstan Labor Code 2025.

items.title: Annual Paid Leave
items.description: Minimum of 24 calendar days per year. Additional days are required for employees in hazardous conditions or for disabled workers.

items.title: Sick Leave Pay
items.description: Employers must pay for the first 15 days of sick leave per year, capped at 25 MCI (~98,300 KZT) per month.

items.title: Maternity Benefits
items.description: Standard leave is 126 calendar days (70 before birth, 56 after). Payment is largely covered by the State Social Insurance Fund.

items.title: Severance Pay
items.description: One month's average salary is mandatory for termination due to redundancy or liquidation.

items.title: Notice Period
items.description: Minimum 1 month written notice is required for most standard employer-initiated terminations. Mutual agreement can bypass this.

items.title: Just Cause Requirement
items.description: Dismissal without just cause is strictly prohibited and often leads to reinstatement and back-pay penalties via labor courts.

items.title: Mutual Agreement
items.description: The safest and most common way to terminate in Kazakhstan is via a signed Mutual Agreement with a negotiated settlement (usually 1-3 months salary).

items.title: Standard Work Week
items.description: 40 hours max. 5-day or 6-day weeks are permitted, but overtime must not exceed 12 hours per month.

items.title: Public Holidays
items.description: 14 public holidays in 2025. If a holiday falls on a weekend, the following Monday is a mandatory day off.

items.title: Remote Work (Enbek)
items.description: Remote work must be explicitly defined in the labor contract and registered on 'Enbek.kz' as such.

items.title: Annual Leave
items.description: Minimum 24 calendar days per year. Unused leave must be compensated upon termination.

items.label: GDP Growth Forecast
items.description: Robust recovery driven by energy sector expansion and mining.

items.label: Inflation Target
items.description: Easing from previous highs, supported by tight monetary policy.

items.label: Unemployment Rate
items.description: Highly stable labor market with strong demand in urban hubs.

items.label: Average Monthly Wage
items.description: Varies significantly between Almaty/Astana and rural regions.

items.title: Hospitality & Rapport
items.description: Business in Kazakhstan is relationship-driven. Initial meetings often involve tea and extended small talk to build personal trust.

items.title: Hierarchical Structure
items.description: Respect for seniority and authority is paramount. Decisions usually flow top-down.

items.title: Indirect Communication
items.description: Softening direct refusals is common. 'We will consider it' often means 'No' or 'Not now'.

items.title: Nauryz Celebrations
items.description: March is dominated by the New Year (Nauryz). Business slows down during the 10-day cultural festival.

items.question: Can I hire foreigners through a Kazakhstan EOR?
items.answer: Yes, but they must obtain a C-type work visa or have a residence permit. EAEU citizens (Russia, Belarus, Armenia, Kyrgyzstan) have simplified access.

items.question: What is the typical management fee for EOR in Kazakhstan?
items.answer: Management fees typically range from $250 to $600 USD per employee per month, depending on the complexity and volume of hires.

items.question: Is the 13th-month salary mandatory?
items.answer: No, a 13th-month salary is not legally required but is common as an annual bonus in sectors like banking and energy.

items.question: What happens if an employee gets sick?
items.answer: Employers pay for the first 15 days using a specific MCI-based formula. Social security covers longer periods.

items.question: Is probation mandatory?
items.answer: Probation is optional but highly recommended. The maximum duration is 3 months for regular staff and 6 months for management.

items.question: Are electronic labor contracts legal?
items.answer: Yes, and they are now mandatory to be registered in the state 'Enbek' system to be considered legally valid.

items.title: Payment Frequency
items.description: Salaries must be paid at least once every month. Many companies use a semi-monthly cycle (Advance + Balance).

items.title: Tax Filing Deadline
items.description: Payroll taxes and social contributions must be remitted by the 25th of the month following the reporting month.

items.title: Reporting Form 200.00
items.description: Quarterly submission of Form 200.00 is mandatory for all employers to report employee income and social taxes.

items.title: Currency Requirement
items.description: Salaries for Kazakhstan residents must be denominated and paid in Tenge (KZT).

items.title: Salary Payment
items.description: Recommended date for final monthly salary payment.

items.title: Tax Remittance
items.description: Deadline for paying PIT, Social Tax, and Pension contributions.

items.title: Q4 2024 Report
items.description: Deadline for Form 200.00 submission for the previous quarter.

items.title: Ecological Allowance
items.text: Employees working in ecologically damaged areas (e.g., Near Semipalatinsk) are entitled to additional pay and leave.

items.title: Shift Premium
items.text: Standard night shift (10 PM to 6 AM) requires at least 1.5x the normal hourly rate.

items.title: Personal Tax Deduction
items.text: Standard deduction of 14 MCI (~55,000 KZT) per month applies to the income tax base for residents.

content.title: Hiring a Senior IT Specialist
content.description: Total cost analysis for a monthly gross salary of 1,500,000 KZT (~$3,200 USD).

items.question: Can I pay employees in USD in Kazakhstan?
items.answer: No. According to the Law on Currency Regulation, residents must be paid in Tenge (KZT). Only non-residents under specific conditions might receive foreign currency.

items.question: Are there different rates for non-residents?
items.answer: Non-residents are generally taxed at a 10% or 15% income tax rate depending on their residency status. Social taxes may vary based on international treaties.

items.question: How is overtime calculated?
items.answer: Overtime is calculated at 1.5x for the first two hours and 2x for subsequent hours or work on weekends/holidays.

items.question: What is the frequency of PIT payments?
items.answer: PIT must be remitted monthly by the 25th of the month following the payment.

items.question: Is salary secrecy protected by law?
items.answer: Yes, employers must maintain confidentiality of personal data, including salary details, under the Data Protection Law.

items.question: Are payroll slips electronic or paper?
items.answer: Both are legal, but electronic slips via email or HR portal are the standard practice in urban business hubs.

steps.title: Determine Gross Salary
steps.description: Start with the agreed monthly gross in KZT.

steps.title: Deduct Health Insurance (OSMS)
steps.description: 2% of gross paid by the employee (capped).

steps.title: Apply Min Wage Deduction
steps.description: Subtract 14 MCI (standard deduction for residents) from the taxable base.

steps.title: Calculate Income Tax (IPN)
steps.description: Apply 10% on the remaining taxable base.

steps.title: Result: Net Take-Home
steps.description: Final amount deposited into the employee's bank account.

items.question: How often does the MCI rate change?
items.answer: The Monthly Calculation Index (MCI) is updated annually by the state budget (4,060 KZT for 2025).

items.question: Does this apply to foreigners?
items.answer: Foreigners from EAEU countries have identical rates. Non-EAEU foreigners may have different pension contribution requirements depending on their residency status.

items.question: What is the 2025 Minimum Salary (MZP)?
items.answer: The Minimum Salary for 2025 is set at 85,000 KZT, which serves as a base for many tax calculations.

items.question: Is there a cap on social contributions?
items.answer: Yes, most contributions are capped at 7 or 10 times the Minimum Salary, preventing excessive tax for high earners.

items.question: Do remote workers have different taxes?
items.answer: No, if they are under a local labor contract, standard rates apply regardless of physical office attendance.

items.question: How is overtime calculated?
items.answer: Overtime must be paid at no less than 1.5x the standard rate, and holiday work at 2.0x, per Art. 108 of the Labor Code.

heroData.title: Incorporation Kazakhstan
heroData.subtitle: LLP (TOO) & AIFC Registration
heroData.description: Establish your presence in Central Asia. From standard Limited Liability Partnerships (TOO) to high-tech AIFC structures with 50-year tax holidays.

steps.title: Corporate Name Reservation
steps.description: Verify and reserve a unique name for the TOO through the National Register of Business Identification Numbers.

steps.title: IIN & EDS Setup
steps.description: Foreign directors must obtain an Individual Identification Number (IIN) and an Electronic Digital Signature (EDS) for online filing.

steps.title: Charter & Articles drafting
steps.description: Develop the company's foundation documents, including the Charter (Ustav) and the Foundation Agreement if multiple partners are involved.

steps.title: State Registration
steps.description: Submit application via eGov.kz or at the Public Service Center (PSC). Registration is typically completed in 1-3 working days for SMEs.

steps.title: Bank Account & Seal
steps.description: Open a local Tenge and multi-currency bank account. While official seals are now optional for some, they remain common for customs.

steps.title: Tax Regime Election
steps.description: Choose between the Simplified Tax Regime (3% on revenue) or the General Regime (20% on profit) within 30 days of registration.

items.title: C3 Work Visa
items.description: The standard visa for foreign employees. Issued for 1-3 years based on a local work permit. AIFC/Hub participants get 5-year multi-entry.

items.title: C5 Business Immigrant
items.description: Mandatory for foreign founders who wish to actively manage their local company (TOO).

items.title: EAEU/CIS Exceptions
items.description: Citizens of Russia, Belarus, Armenia, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan only need a Temporary Residence Permit (RVP), not a work visa.

items.title: B10 Private Visa
items.description: Used for short-term business visits but does not grant the right to engage in long-term local employment.

items.title: AIFC (Special Zone)
items.text: Operates under English Common Law. Ideal for financial services and tech. CIT/VAT exemptions available until 2066 for priority activities.

items.title: TOO (Mainland LLP)
items.text: Standard legal form under Civil Law. Simple to manage, low minimum capital (often zero for SMEs), and widely accepted for trading and services.

items.title: Branch/Representation
items.text: Easiest for foreign companies to set up for marketing or support. Not a separate legal entity, taxed based on local revenue.

items.title: Legal Address
items.description: A valid physical office space lease or property certificate is required for registration. Virtual offices are increasingly scrutinized by tax authorities.

items.title: State Inspection Access
items.description: Offices must be accessible to fire safety and san-epidemic inspectors, especially in industrial zones.

items.title: Localized Signage
items.description: Company name on the office door must be in Kazakh and Russian languages per the Language Law.

items.question: Can a 100% foreign-owned company open a TOO?
items.answer: Yes, foreign individuals and legal entities can have 100% ownership of a Kazakhstan TOO without a local partner.

items.question: Do I need to visit Kazakhstan to open a company?
items.answer: Initial IIN/EDS setup usually requires a visit or a Power of Attorney. The actual registration can be done remotely via the e-Gov portal once IDs are secured.

items.question: What is the C5 Business Immigrant Visa?
items.answer: It is a mandatory visa for foreign citizens who wish to be the founder/director of a local company. It requires a criminal record check and health certificate.

items.question: How long does it take to open a bank account?
items.answer: Typically 3-7 working days after registration, depending on the bank's KYC requirements for foreign UBOs.

items.question: Are there annual renewal fees?
items.answer: There is no 'annual license fee' for a TOO, but companies must file quarterly and annual tax reports to remain active.

items.question: Can a TOO have multiple directors?
items.answer: Yes, but usually one 'General Director' is the primary authorized signatory. Joint signing powers can be defined in the Charter.

heroData.title: Staffing Kazakhstan
heroData.subtitle: Top Talent Acquisition
heroData.description: Connecting global businesses with Kazakhstan's skilled workforce. Specialized recruitment for the Almaty tech hub and the AIFC financial ecosystem.

items.title: Almaty
items.text: The cultural and commercial heart. Houses 70% of the country's software developers and creative agencies.

items.title: Astana
items.text: The administrative capital. Prime location for government-facing roles, AIFC financial experts, and the Astana Hub tech ecosystem.

items.title: Atyrau & Aktau
items.text: Strategic centers for the Oil & Gas sector and engineering specialists.

items.title: HeadHunter.kz (HH)
items.description: The dominant professional job board for white-collar and management roles in Kazakhstan.

items.title: Enbek.kz
items.description: The national state platform, vital for reporting and broad labor market reach.

items.title: LinkedIn
items.description: Gaining traction for IT and senior executive recruitment in Almaty and Astana.

items.title: Telegram Channels
items.description: Hyper-local tech and creative communities used for rapid recruitment and freelance sourcing.

items.title: Health Insurance (VHI)
items.description: Voluntary Health Insurance is the #1 requested benefit for skilled talent in Kazakhstan.

items.title: Training Budgets
items.description: Access to international certifications (AWS, PMP, CFA) is highly valued by the ambitious younger workforce.

items.title: Work-Life Balance
items.description: Flexible hours and remote work options are now standard expectations in the tech sector.

items.title: Oil & Gas Demand
items.text: The Tengiz expansion project is expected to create 22,000 technical jobs by 2025-2026.

items.title: Nuclear Energy
items.text: New power plant projects are projected to add 5,000 operational roles by 2030.

items.title: Technical Skill Gap
items.text: High demand for specialized petroleum engineers and project managers often requires expat sourcing or rapid local re-skilling.

items.title: Background Checks
items.description: Criminal record checks (Police Certificates) can be obtained via eGov but require the candidate's explicit digital consent.

items.title: Degree Verification
items.description: Verification of diplomas is recommended, as fraudulent credentials remain a localized risk in some sectors.

items.title: Data Privacy
items.description: Handling of recruitment data must comply with the Kazakhstan Law on Personal Data protection.

items.question: How long does it take to fill a role?
items.answer: Typical time-to-hire in Almaty is 4-6 weeks for technical roles and 2-3 weeks for administrative positions.

items.question: What are the common benefits expected by employees?
items.answer: Private medical insurance, mobile allowance, and performance bonuses are standard for white-collar roles in larger cities.

items.question: Is remote work popular in Kazakhstan?
items.answer: Since 2020, remote work has been legally codified and is very common in the IT sector, though many traditional companies prefer a hybrid approach.

items.question: What is the notice period for resignations?
items.answer: Standard notice period for employees is 1 month, unless a longer period is specified in the labor contract.

items.question: Are there quotas for hiring foreign workers?
items.answer: Yes, unless you are in a special zone like AIFC or hiring citizens of EAEU countries, you must comply with government-set foreign labor quotas.

items.question: What is the average probation period?
items.answer: Usually 3 months. During this time, either party can terminate with 3 days' notice if performance is unsatisfactory.

heroData.title: Software Solutions Kazakhstan
heroData.subtitle: Digital Ecosystem Mastery
heroData.description: Implementing and localizing business software for the Central Asian market. Expertise in Kaspi integration, ERP systems, and cloud localization.

items.title: Super App Dominance
items.text: Kaspi.kz is the primary tool for retail, B2B payments, and tax filing. Software solutions must often integrate with this ecosystem.

items.title: GovTech Leadership
items.text: Kazakhstan ranks high in E-Government. Systems like e-SFF (invoicing) and Enbek (labor) are API-driven and mandatory for business.

items.title: 1C Enterprise
items.description: The core ERP and accounting backbone for localized businesses, with specialized modules for Kazakh taxation.

items.title: Cloud Computing
items.description: Increasing adoption of Microsoft Azure and local providers like Kaztelecom for on-soil data storage, ensuring compliance with localization laws.

items.title: API Integrations
items.description: Mandatory integration with the state 'Smart Data Ukimet' and 'E-Invoicing' (ESF) systems for real-time reporting.

items.question: Is there a local SaaS market?
items.answer: Yes, Almaty and Astana Hub host hundreds of SaaS startups focusing on CRM, retail, and fleet management localized for Central Asia.

items.question: What are the cybersecurity requirements?
items.answer: Businesses must follow state standards for information security, especially if handling citizen IDs (IINs) and banking data.

items.question: Can we host our data on AWS/GCP?
items.answer: Yes, but personal data of Kazakhstani citizens MUST be stored on a local mirror or primary server within Kazakhstan territory.

items.question: Is open-source software common in gov projects?
items.answer: Yes, the government promotes the use of open-source to reduce licensing costs and enhance sovereignty.

items.question: How do we integrate with 'Enbek.kz'?
items.answer: Enbek provides rest APIs for HRIS systems to automate the registration of labor contracts and social contributions.

items.question: What is the 'Digital Tenge'?
items.answer: The National Bank is piloting a Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) to streamline B2B and gov payments, expected for full release by late 2025.

heroData.title: Marketing Kazakhstan
heroData.subtitle: Growth & Localization
heroData.description: Drive demand in Central Asia through curated marketing strategies. Focus on Instagram-heavy social commerce and bilingual consumer trends.

items.title: Visual-First Economy
items.text: High-quality video content and Reels on Instagram/TikTok are the primary drivers of B2C conversion.

items.title: Bilingualism
items.text: Content must be localized into Kazakh and Russian. The use of Kazakh is rapidly increasing in marketing for younger demographics.

items.title: Instagram & TikTok
items.description: The most effective platforms for reaching the tech-savvy urban population of Almaty and Astana.

items.title: Influencer Marketing
items.description: Highly developed ecosystem with micro-influencers yielding high ROI for niche B2B and B2C brands.

items.title: Contextual Ads
items.description: Google Ads remains vital, while Yandex Direct is also used for specific industrial sectors.

items.question: What is the 'influencer tax'?
items.answer: Since 2024, influencers must register as taxpayers and clearly label their advertising content to comply with new media laws.

items.question: Is email marketing effective?
items.answer: B2B email marketing is standard, but B2C consumers strongly prefer messengers (WhatsApp/Telegram) for brand interaction.

items.question: What are the rules for outdoor advertising?
items.answer: Placement requires permits from the local 'Akimat' (municipality) and must strictly comply with language laws (Kazakh always on top/left).

items.question: Can we run ads in English?
items.answer: English is allowed but must be accompanied by Kazakh and Russian translations, except for registered trademarks.

items.question: How popular is YouTube in Kazakhstan?
items.answer: Extremely. localized Kazakh-language YouTube content (mini-series, talk shows) is a prime spot for mid-roll sponsorships.

items.question: Is Google and Meta advertising stable?
items.answer: Yes, although payments must often be routed through local agencies to ensure tax compliance with the 'Digital Services VAT'.
